filtered_findings.description: pdu_408_build() appends the payload marker with `pdu->token[pdu->used_size++] = COAP_PAYLOAD_START;` without any capacity check, and ignores the return value of the preceding coap_add_option_internal(COAP_OPTION_CONTENT_TYPE) call. coap_add_token() accepts a token whenever `len + bias <= pdu->max_size`, so a token can legitimately bring `used_size` exactly to `alloc_size` (which equals `max_size` on UDP, where `max_size = mtu - 4` and the initial allocation is `min(size, COAP_DEFAULT_MTU)`); the content-format option (3 bytes for value 272) then fails coap_pdu_check_resize() because growing would exceed `max_size`, but that failure is ignored and the payload marker is written at `token[alloc_size]`, i.e. exactly one byte past the end of the `alloc_size + max_hdr_size` heap buffer. This is a static-analysis candidate; the ASan/UBSan instrumented fuzzing performed during this review did not exercise this exact size/token combination, so the defect is not dynamically confirmed.
filtered_findings.exploit_scenario: A server built with Q-Block support (enabled by default) and with RFC 8974 extended tokens enabled by the application (e.g. coap-server -T / coap_context_set_max_token_size() with a value > 8) receives a Q-Block1 request whose token length is chosen as `coap_session_max_pdu_size() - 2` (for a default UDP MTU of 1152 the PDU size is 1148, so a 1146-byte extended token). The attacker then delivers Q-Block1 payload blocks out of order (or omits an early block) so that coap_request_missing_q_block1() calls pdu_408_build() for the 4.08 Missing-Blocks response. The token fills the PDU to capacity, the Content-Format option is silently dropped, and the unchecked marker write places 0xFF one byte past the heap allocation, corrupting the adjacent allocator chunk. The attacker can repeat this per session.
filtered_findings.recommendation: Do not write the payload marker unconditionally. Check the result of coap_add_option_internal() and call coap_pdu_check_resize(pdu, pdu->used_size + 1) before writing the marker; if the option or the resize fails, delete the PDU and return NULL (the caller already handles a NULL return by deferring the 4.08). Alternatively route the marker prepend through coap_add_data_after()/coap_add_data(), which perform the required bounds check.

_filter_metadata.justification: Concrete memory-safety issue in C code (not covered by the Rust exclusion). The finding describes a specific 1-byte heap out-of-bounds write at line 1879 in pdu_408_build(), with a plausible mechanism: coap_add_token() can bring used_size to alloc_size, the Content-Format option add fails resize but its failure is ignored, and the payload marker is written unconditionally one byte past the buffer. This has a clear attack path (Q-Block1 request with a max-length extended token delivered out of order). It is not dynamically confirmed and depends on the application enabling extended tokens (>8), which reduces exploitability but does not make it a false positive. Worth investigating and fixing with a bounds check.
